title: Cerebral venous thrombosis: anticoagulation
keyNumbers: Enoxaparin (treatment dose): 1 mg/kg SC q12h (CrCl <30: 1 mg/kg daily)
After the acute phase: VKA (INR 2.0–3.0) for 3–12 months depending on cause; indefinitely with thrombophilia or recurrent VTE
CVT during pregnancy: Full-dose LMWH throughout pregnancy, then LMWH or VKA ≥6 weeks postpartum (total ≥3 months)

Suspected VITT (after adenovirus-vector vaccine, thrombocytopenia): Send PF4 antibodies; avoid all heparin; IVIG 1 g/kg daily × 2 days; steroids; no platelet transfusion; argatroban or fondaparinux, then DOAC after platelet recovery
question: How is CVT anticoagulated, for how long, and when to escalate?
population: Confirmed cerebral venous thrombosis in adults

rules.recommendation: Parenteral heparin first; LMWH favored over UFH

rules.condition: Venous (hemorrhagic) infarct or ICH at presentation

rules.recommendation: VKA (INR 2.0–3.0) for 3–12 months depending on cause; indefinitely with thrombophilia or recurrent VTE

rules.condition: Considering a DOAC instead of VKA
rules.recommendation: DOACs appear safe and effective (RE-SPECT CVT: dabigatran after 5–15 days of parenteral lead-in); avoid in pregnancy, breastfeeding and antiphospholipid syndrome
Full-dose LMWH throughout pregnancy, then LMWH or VKA ≥6 weeks postpartum (total ≥3 months)
Using recanalization on CTV/MRV to set duration remains uncertain

rules.condition: Thrombus propagation, deterioration despite medical therapy, or contraindication to anticoagulation
rules.recommendation: Consider endovascular therapy (no controlled studies; poorer outcomes in meta-analyses)
Decompressive surgery — lifesaving and may improve function
Send PF4 antibodies; avoid all heparin; IVIG 1 g/kg daily × 2 days; steroids; no platelet transfusion; argatroban or fondaparinux, then DOAC after platelet recovery

notes: UFH if procedure or surgery likely
evidenceNote: Dose: Lovenox label §2.2 (1 mg/kg q12h) and §2.3 Table 1 (CrCl <30: 1 mg/kg daily)

pearls: Hemorrhage is present in up to 40% of CVT (Saposnik 2024)
Saposnik 2024 is an ungraded scientific statement; the ESO 2017 CVT guideline (graded) is not stored
sources: Saposnik G, et al. Diagnosis and Management of Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Scientific Statement From the AHA. Stroke 2024;55:e77-e90. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000456
